item.description: I can still remember how different that gold cartridge felt from every other Nintendo game I owned. Before I even pressed Start, The Legend of Zelda already felt like something important. As a kid, I would sit on the floor way too close to the TV and disappear into Hyrule for hours. Most of the time I had absolutely no idea where I was going. I burned random bushes, bombed every wall that looked suspicious and wandered around as Link hoping I would accidentally discover a hidden cave, a new item or another piece of the Triforce. There were no easy answers. You learned secrets from a friend at school, scribbled notes on paper and raced home to see if the rumor was actually true. Every discovery felt like it belonged to you. The Legend of Zelda was released in the US 39 years ago today, and I can still hear that opening music in my head. That original NES game did not just feel like something I played. It felt like my own adventure. Who else remembers seeing that gold cartridge for the first time?

item.title: Void screaming
item.description: She and I have been in couples therapy for a while now, we both are in individual therapy as well. She does things like not invite my eldest to play board games, doesn't tell her when it's food time stating she is 18 she can figure out what to eat and eat on her own time. (We always all eat supper together every single day.) Generally does small things that make my eldest not feel like she is welcome to live in this house. She blames me for 100% of our communication issues, even though it is 1 thing that I do that gets to her, and even then haven't done it since it was brought to light that she didn't like it. I've been trying to speak to her the last few days and she's given the cold shoulder and single word responses, and yells at me for not trying to speak to her. I've tried many times. I even wrote out a full letter to her expressing how I felt about what is currently going on, and was told that it isn't acceptable to speak that way. Even though she won't hold a conversation with me. I don't have a job, haven't worked in over 10 years due to health issues. I have a VA pension but it doesn't cover the bills. I've been looking because her current job doesn't offer any weekends off. And that is now the only time she has her kids. That also means (with the job im interviewing for) that i am going to be losing out on time with my kids. She's going to stay with family. And we are getting a divorce. I am afraid of losing my house because I have no place to turn too, and renting a place would be more expensive than the sweet deal I have on my mortgage for this house. I don't have a savings, I can't afford a divorce lawyer and my pension is too much to get legal aid. I'm fucked. Edit Pool added by suggestion. I hate doing it. But any little bit helps. I know it's 5k to retain a lawyer here. So will be saving to that as quick as I can, while still looking at other options like legal aide and pro bono. https://www.paypal.com/pool/9s0X0pBPmQ?sr=accr Edit 2: surprised this made most viral. They really set the bar low these days don't they. Thank you everyone.
